title: Parser resilience for escaped JSON and mixed-format tool outputs causing production hangs
creator: Anika Rao
description: Several customers across Hosted and Dedicated reported production requests where tool/function call outputs containing escaped JSON fragments or mixed text+json payloads trapped the structured-output parser. Symptoms varied: streaming responses stalled after emitting partial tool output, synchronous requests returned HTTP 500 with 'parse_error', and occasional duplication of KV-cache prefixes when fallback model variants returned different quoting conventions. The issue is customer-impacting because it affects market-facing assistants that rely on strict tool return shapes and leads to degraded UX and increased error rates in downstream processing.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use hosted API with function/tool calling enabled and a tool that returns a nested JSON payload embedded in a string field (e.g., "{\"id\": 123, \"meta\": \"{\\\"x\\\": 1}\"}").
2) Send the request with streaming=true and a short response budget so the runtime uses standard chunking behaviour.

3) Observe that the client receives a truncated chunk ending inside the escaped JSON and the server logs show a parser exception followed by worker thread backpressure leading to increased latency for subsequent requests.

4) Repeat with Dedicated node set using a different model variant; sometimes model fallback returns single-quotes or unescaped braces which causes the structured parser to treat payload as malformed and escalate to a 500 path.
logs_and_evidence: customer: AcmeAI, request_id: 2026-02-24T14:12:03Z, server-log snippet: parser.go:245 parse_error: unmatched quote at offset 432
customer: FinLex, observed behaviour: streaming socket closed by server after chunk id 8, client saw 100% duplication for chunks 4-7 on retry
investigation_notes: Initial triage: parser assumes tool outputs are either raw JSON tokens or plain text; it fails when both appear inside the same token while streaming boundaries split escapes.
Reproducer created in sandbox that simulates streaming split inside an escaped backslash sequence; confirmed parser throws 'unterminated escape' error.

Root cause (summary): streaming chunk boundaries + naive unescape step in structured parser. When a chunk ends inside a "\\" sequence we attempt to unescape before full token arrives leading to invalid state. Secondary contributor: fallback model variants returning inconsistent quoting/shallow-serialization increased freq. of failures in Dedicated clusters using routing fallback.
KV-cache duplication traced to retry code path combined with early parser abort: memory of partial prefixes was re-applied when worker returned to queue without proper cursor reset.
decisions: 1) Implement chunk-safe streaming parser that buffers incomplete escape sequences until token boundary is seen (short-term hotfix for hosted).
2) Add canonicalizer in the runtime that normalizes tool returns before structured-parse attempt (escape normalization + enforced JSON schema check).
3) Patch retry/worker return path to always reset KV-cache cursor on parser abort to prevent duplication.
4) Schedule Dedicated/Private rollout as a minor runtime package (runtime-1.22.1) with opt-in flag initially; then auto-enable after 2 days of host metrics stability.
